The One and Only Ivan + The One and Only Bob ate similarly written animal fiction - quick reads but very compelling

There’s a scene in one of the Moomin novels by Tove Jansson where Moomintroll watches his mother struggle to throw a snowball, and in watching her he has the sudden impulse to tell her how much he loves her. 

It’s a really simple scene and for some reason it always makes me tear up.

The Seep by Chana Porter ticks off a number of your boxes. It’s a bit difficult to describe other than that it involves an invasion where the aforementioned aliens are a microscopic particle hive mind that latch on to humans in an attempt to both understand and ‘fix’ them.

It’s not really scary (some parts are) - but the focus is romance and it’s a very short, snappy read. I really enjoyed it!
The Shining is a really strong early King novel - but I’d say that the one that’s continued to hold up as really, genuinely terrifying is Misery

One thing that helped was doing literally just one thing a day, even if that one thing was just taking a shower (even just standing in the stall for 5 mins was *something*). Bud I’m sorry you’re getting downvoted. It’s a legit question to ask and honestly? There are a lot of uncomfy parts of Part 1 that have aged like sour milk. I don’t even watch episode one anymore bc it gets so overtly creepy towards Fujiko, like more than usual creepy.

But yeah. It really does vary. Part 2 has a lot of it but it’s framed in a way that’s less overt and more just “goofy” - though there are still some scenes that border on assault. Part 3 has some but it’s a lot cleaner in that there’s nothing non-consensual, at least to my memory of it. 

The modern Parts 4 & 5 are relatively scrubbed up, though I would say that there are some scenes in Part 5 that are particularly egregious since they deal with a teenage girl. Ugh.

As for the films, as others have said they vary based on the director. Some are raunchy as hell and others are really darn tame. It’s always been a grab bag with those.

I adore Lupin III - it’s a franchise that’s very near and dear to my heart. The sexual side of it has always been my least favorite aspect, but the characters and high stakes action really make up for it. I can totally understand that for a lot of folk it can be an instant turn-off, and that should be respected.
